Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Intake Brief: Follow-on-Steam incentive — unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher

## Problem statement

The upcoming Steam release of the Tableau Card Engine launcher (Electron) needs a growth mechanic: when a player follows the game/developer on Steam, they receive one of the bundled example games for free. The mechanic must feel seamless — the Steam store page opens automatically (player already logged in), they follow, and the launcher detects the follow and unlocks the bonus game.

## Users

- **Steam players** — get a free game as an incentive to follow the TCE Steam presence; discover the engine's games.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — grow Steam following/wishlists and reward engaged players without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want to click "Follow us on Steam" in the launcher and have the store page open automatically (already logged in), so following takes one click.
- As a Steam player, I want the bonus game to unlock in my launcher once I've followed, so I can play it immediately.
- As a publisher, I want the free-game unlock to be delivered through the existing bundled-content/DLC architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The launcher shows a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action (e.g. a small panel/button) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client/overlay via Steamworks (player is already logged in — no browser login prompt).
2. After the player follows, the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks and unlocks the designated bonus game (one of the existing example games) in the launcher's game list; verified by an end-to-end check with a real Steam account (manual QA) and, where feasible, a mocked Steamworks session in automated tests.
3. The unlock persists across launches (player who followed once keeps the game; no re-verification prompt on every boot).
4. The bonus game is delivered as part of the bundled-content architecture (locked by default) so no separate download is needed; the unlock mechanism is game-agnostic (works for whichever game is designated as the bonus).
5. If the Steam client/Steamworks is unavailable (e.g. dev environment, non-Steam launch), the launcher must not crash: the CTA degrades gracefully (hidden or "follow via browser" fallback) and the web app remains fully functional.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Electron** launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; this feature integrates Steamworks SDK into that launcher (explicitly deferred scope of the launcher item — this item introduces it).
- **Bonus game is bundled** (answer to intake Q: "a game currently in the example games", delivered via the bundled/subset content in the launcher, unlocked in place) — not a separate download.
- **Steam store page via Steamworks** (intake Q3): the CTA opens the store page in the Steam client; follow detection must use the Steamworks SDK and/or Steam Web API.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).
- **Game-agnostic:** the unlock logic must not hard-code the specific bonus game title (the designated game is a business decision, see Appendix).

## Existing state

- Launcher item CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (intake_complete) delivers the Electron binary that boots the Vite web app; scope explicitly defers Steamworks SDK integration ("No Steamworks SDK integration in v1. The launcher must not require Steam to run locally during development.").
- Launcher content-loading is designed so Steam DLC directories can be read (option a) with structure permitting later Steamworks-managed paths (option b) without a rewrite — the follow-unlock must slot into this abstraction.
- The web app (Game Selector) currently lists all example games; the launcher will bundle a subset.
- No Steamworks SDK, Steam app ID, or Steam-related code exists in the repo today.

## Desired change

1. Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron launcher (init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap), keeping the launcher runnable without Steam during development.
2. Add a "Follow us on Steam" CTA (in launcher UI, e.g. Game Selector screen or settings) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client — candidate mechanisms: `SteamFriends()->ActivateGameOverlayToStore(appId, ...)` in the Steamworks SDK, or `steam://openurl`/`steam://store/<appid>` external URL from Electron.
3. Detect the follow and unlock the bonus game. **Research required:** Steam's client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call; candidates to verify during implementation:
   - `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account steamID>)` — client-side check that the user follows the *developer/publisher account* (works without a backend).
   - Steam Web API (`IPlayerService` family, e.g. followed-games queries) — verifies game-page follows but needs a server component and publisher API key.
   - Whichever mechanism is chosen must be verified against the actual Steam account model (game-page follow vs developer-account follow) before committing.
4. Unlock persistence: store a local unlock flag (or Steam-follow state) so the player isn't re-prompted; re-check on demand (e.g. "Refresh" or on follow confirmation).
5. Graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent: CTA hidden or browser fallback; web app unaffected.
6. Tests + docs: mock Steamworks session for automated unlock-logic tests where feasible; manual end-to-end QA with a real Steam account documented in the test plan.

## Key Files

- `electron/main.ts` (new) — Steamworks init, Steam app ID bootstrap, store-page open handler, follow-check orchestration.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` (new) — follow detection + unlock persistence logic (game-agnostic), behind a small interface so the web renderer doesn't depend on the Steam SDK directly.
- `electron/preload.ts` (new) — expose a minimal follow/unlock API to the renderer via context bridge.
- `src/ui/` or launcher UI module — "Follow us on Steam" CTA component (SLL-compliant placement), unlock state display.
- `package.json` — Steamworks SDK dependency (or native module) and scripts; electron-builder config for the Steam distribution.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `RELEASE.md` — document the Steamworks build/QA workflow.
- `AGENTS.md` — note new scripts/requirements if tooling changes.
- `tests/` — unit tests for unlock/persistence logic with a mocked follow source; manual E2E test plan for real-Steam verification.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, intake_complete) — prerequisite: the launcher this feature extends. Its AC #4 (DLC/content-location architecture) must be honored; this feature introduces the deferred Steamworks scope.
- `docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — card-game genre research incl. Steam platform notes (context only).
- No other Steam/Steamworks work items exist (verified via `wl search steam`, `steamworks`, `DLC`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The Steam app (App ID) and developer/publisher Steam account exist outside this repo; this item integrates with them.
- **Assumption:** The designated bonus game is a business decision (TBD — see Appendix) and does not change the technical design (game-agnostic unlock).
- **Assumption:** Following is checked once (on CTA completion) and persisted locally; unfollow-after-unlock is not detected/penalised in v1 (anti-abuse is out of scope).
- **Risk (HIGH):** Steam's client SDK may not expose a reliable client-side "followed this game page" check. Mitigation: implementation begins with a short research spike (candidate APIs above); fallback is developer-account follow via `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, or a small web-API verification if acceptable. This may change the UX (e.g. follow developer account instead of game page) — confirm with user before committing to a fallback.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module adds build complexity to electron-builder packaging and must not break non-Steam dev runs — mitigated by graceful-degradation AC (AC5).
- **Risk:** Electron + Steamworks native module (Steam SDK) packaging on Windows must be validated (steam_appid.txt, app id bootstrap, `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which game is being released on Steam? The TCE is an engine — are we releasing a specific game built on it (e.g., Main Street), or is this about the engine itself?" — Answer (user): "A launcher with a subset of the example games bundled and the ability to add more later (DLC)." Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Steam "release" is the launcher product (per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW); this item is a mechanic in that launcher.
- Q2: "What's the 'free game' offer? When a player follows, they receive a free game — is that a specific existing game from the TCE catalog, a bonus game, or something else?" — Answer (user): "it will be a game currently in the example games." Source: interactive reply. The specific game title is **not yet chosen (OPEN QUESTION for the business)**; ACs are game-agnostic.
- Q3: "How does the Steam integration work: store page with follow-to-unlock via Steamworks API, manual key-claim flow, or something else?" — Answer (user): "Steam store page via Steamworks." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "What platform does the launcher target?" — Answer (user): "desktop (we will be using electron, another item covers this, add requirements there if necessary, see CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW)". Source: interactive reply. Decision: Electron stack already scoped in CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; no requirements added to that item (its scope explicitly defers Steamworks — this feature introduces it and is linked as dependent).
- Q5: "What does 'follow us on Steam' mean technically? Steam has no direct follow webhook..." (options: web flow with in-game store open + API check; code redemption; community group) — Answer (user): "I have played a game that automatically opened the steam store page, I was already logged in and I was following the page. I don't know how they did it, but that's what I want." Source: interactive reply. This is the target UX; the exact Steamworks mechanism is a research spike for implementation (see Risks). Likely components: `ActivateGameOverlayToStore` (or `steam://store/<appid>`) to open the page + a follow-state check.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which example game is the designated free follow-bonus? (business decision; doesn't block technical design — AC4 is game-agnostic.)
- OPEN QUESTION: Follow verification mechanism — game-page follow (needs Steam Web API / backend) vs developer-account follow (`ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, client-side). Must be researched and confirmed with user before implementation commits to a fallback.

## Related work (automated find-related report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSI4IP6A000N7YF** – Coloretto: align player collections (hands) regardless of name/score length (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated game feature)*.
- **CG-0MQH81RIS0017K94** – Coloretto Phaser scene (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.
- **CG-0MROXIJZ3004VGUI** – GymTokenPileView: card-back pile shows 'not found' texture (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-...` — the draft itself (self-match).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (+ a worktree copy) — generic terms (game, feature, store); context only, no Steam-specific content.

> Note: The genuinely related item **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW** (Electron launcher) is covered in the manual Related work section above.

# Intake Brief: Challenges as achievements — sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements

## Problem statement

The engine's challenge system (per-run meta-goals, e.g. Main Street's "Foodie Row") is conceptually a form of achievement. Once the Steam version exists (Electron launcher with Steamworks), challenge completions should sync to Steam achievements so players earn persistent, account-level recognition visible on their Steam profile and in the overlay.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn Steam achievements for completing in-game challenges; see progress on their Steam profile.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — an engine-generic achievement layer so any game can map its challenges to Steam achievements without writing Steam SDK code.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want the challenges I complete in Main Street (and future games) to appear as Steam achievements, so my progress is recognised beyond the run itself.
- As a TCE developer, I want a game-agnostic achievement layer in the engine, so adding achievements to a new game is declarative (challenge → achievement mapping) with no Steam SDK code in the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An **engine-generic achievement layer** exists in the core engine (extending the existing generic `ChallengeSystem` model): games define achievement definitions (id, title, description, hidden flag) and map challenge completions to achievements. This layer is pure engine code with no Steam dependency (works headless / in the web build).
2. When a challenge is completed inside the Steam launcher, the mapped Steam achievement is unlocked via Steamworks (`ISteamUserStats::SetAchievement` + `StoreStats`); verified by automated tests with a mocked Steamworks session and a documented manual E2E check with a real Steam account.
3. Steam sync is **idempotent and offline-safe**: unlocked achievements persist locally, are re-synced to Steam when available, and the launcher never crashes when Steam/Steamworks is absent (graceful degradation, consistent with the follow-on-Steam feature CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
4. A single **achievement manifest** (game id ↔ achievement id ↔ Steam API name, hidden flag) is the source of truth and matches the static Steam store configuration; mismatch detection is documented.
5. **Main Street is the first consumer**: all 12 challenge templates (`MainStreetChallenges.ts`) are mapped to Steam achievements through the generic layer (no Steam SDK code in the game module).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Timing:** Steam sync is implemented only when the Steam version exists — blocked by the Electron launcher (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) and the Steamworks integration introduced by the follow-on-Steam incentive (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC). The engine-generic achievement layer itself can be designed/built now; the Steam bridge lands with Steamworks.
- **Engine-generic (user decision):** no game-specific Steam code; games declare achievements via the generic layer; Main Street first.
- **Steam backend reality:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steam store backend with static API names (App ID + achievement list). The manifest must match that configuration; store setup itself lives outside this repo.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies (Steamworks SDK usage follows the pattern set by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).

## Existing state

- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` / `ActiveChallengeRecord<TState>` interfaces plus generic selection/evaluation; game-agnostic by design ("M6 extraction" notes already anticipate reuse).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — the only consumer: 12 challenge templates across 5 categories, per-run selection (`selectChallenges`), evaluation with completion callback that pushes to `state.challengesCompleted` and the activity log. Challenges are run-local and non-persistent.
- No achievements, no Steam SDK code, no Electron code in the repo today. Steamworks integration is being introduced by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC into the launcher from CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW.
- CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC explicitly defers this scope: "Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item."

## Desired change

1. Add an **achievement concept to the core engine** (new module, e.g. `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`, or an extension of `ChallengeSystem`): achievement definitions, a completion-event surface, and a persistence-agnostic "unlock" registry that the web build can use without Steam.
2. Define the **achievement manifest** for the launcher (`electron/steam-achievements.ts`): game/achievement ids ↔ Steam API names + hidden flags, documented to match the Steam store backend config.
3. Add the **Steam bridge** in the Electron main process: renderer reports achievement-unlocked events via preload/IPC; main process calls Steamworks `SetAchievement`/`StoreStats`; local persistence of unlocked ids with later re-sync; graceful degradation without Steam.
4. **Wire Main Street** as the first consumer: a declarative mapping from the 12 challenge templates to Steam achievements, fired from the existing challenge-completion path.
5. Tests (mocked Steamworks session; headless unit tests for the engine layer) + documentation (README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md` as needed).

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts` (new) — generic achievement definitions + unlock registry + completion-event surface (no Steam dependency).
- `src/core-engine/index.ts` — barrel exports for the new module.
- `electron/steam-achievements.ts` (new) — achievement manifest (ids ↔ Steam API names) + Steamworks sync bridge.
- `electron/main.ts`, `electron/preload.ts` — IPC surface for achievement-unlock events from the renderer.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` (or a new `MainStreetAchievements.ts`) — mapping of the 12 challenge templates to achievements.
- `tests/` — unit tests (engine layer, manifest matching) + mocked-Steamworks sync tests.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md` — Steam achievements workflow documentation.

## Related work

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn free games as a reward for reaching achievements; a reason to keep playing.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — a growth/engagement mechanic that drives play without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want a free game to unlock in my launcher once I've won my first game and reached one more milestone, so my progress is rewarded.

2. Each give-away game unlocks when the player achieves its configured trigger achievements: **"win your first game" plus one additional achievement** (suggested: first win in a second distinct game — final choice recorded, see Appendix). 3. The unlock uses **the same mechanism as the follow-on-Steam free game** (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC): bundled content, locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches, game-agnostic unlock logic.

## Summary

The F1-approved follow-detection mechanism — `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(developerSteamID)` — is **not exposed** by `steamworks.js`, the only maintained npm binding for the Steamworks SDK (verified: v0.4.0 exposes achievement/apps/auth/cloud/input/localplayer/matchmaking/networking/overlay/stats/utils/workshop namespaces, but **no `friends` namespace**).

As a result, the launcher shipped on CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC implements:
- real SDK store-page opening via `overlay.activateToStore` / `activateToWebPage`,
- real Steamworks init (`init` + `restartAppIfNecessary` + app id bootstrap),
- follow detection **capability-detected**: `followCheckSupported = false` when the binding lacks the API, with a persisted **manual self-attest claim** fallback.

This delivers the feature with graceful degradation, but does **not** achieve fully automatic follow detection.

## Desired outcome

Automatic follow detection that survives an audit of intake AC2 ("the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks"), via one of:

- (a) A small **custom native addon** wrapping `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` (N-API), shipped alongside `steamworks.js`; the existing `SteamworksClientLike.friends.isFollowing` seam means no TypeScript change is needed once present.
- (b) A newer `steamworks.js` release (or a fork) that exposes `friends.isFollowing`.
- (c) A publisher-backend Steam Web API check (needs a server component; previously scoped out).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A concrete mechanism exposing `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` is available to the Electron main process.
- [ ] `SteamworksFollowSource.followCheckSupported` becomes `true` on a real Steam session and automatic unlock is verified end-to-end with a real Steam account.
- [ ] No regression to the graceful-degradation path (absent module → unavailable, no crash).
- [ ] Automated tests cover the new detection path with a fake module.

## Relationship

Discovered while implementing CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC (F3). Follow-up, not a blocker: the shipped feature degrades to a manual claim.

## Goal

On a **real Windows x64 machine with the Steam client**, validate end-to-end that the Option A native addon (`native/steam-friends`) enables **automatic** Steam follow detection, that the bonus game unlocks without a manual claim, and that every degradation path is safe. This is the operator-run validation for the epic **`CG-0MUN7930Y009X8Z1`** (implementation P1–P5 are complete on `dev`); executing this runbook produces the evidence that satisfies **P6 `CG-0MUNBI08A001D0XU`** and parent AC2.

**Discovered from:** `CG-0MUN7930Y009X8Z1` (epic). **Complements:** P6 `CG-0MUNBI08A001D0XU` (epic verification child). **Reference plan:** `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md`.

## What was built (the thing being validated)

Serial implementation already on `dev`:

| Item | Commit | Delivered |
|------|--------|-----------|
| P1 `CG-0MUNBHWY90051NAU` | `64367e0c` | Spike report `docs/dev/steam-follow-native-spike.md` |
| P2 `CG-0MUNBHXMC00192G8` | `b56c0ef4` | Loader seam (`nativeFriendsLoader`, `followCheckTimeoutMs`) + fake-module tests |
| P3 `CG-0MUNBHYAB0011XXW` | `1835d882` | C++ N-API addon (`native/steam-friends`) + `electron/steam-follow-native.ts` |
| P4 `CG-0MUNBHYY0001PHKU` | `fb5e5bd5` | Packaging (`electron-builder.yml`), `scripts/build-steam-friends.mjs`, `scripts/check-steam-friends.mjs`, `package:steam` |
| P5 `CG-0MUNBHZL3006UK6U` | `4d6e0aa2` | Docs, licensing, QA plan |

Mechanism: `steamworks.js` 0.4.0 exposes no `friends.isFollowing`, so the addon finds the `steam_api64.dll` **already loaded by `steamworks.js`**, calls `SteamAPI_ISteamFriends_IsFollowing` (interface `SteamFriends017`), and correlates the asynchronous `FriendsIsFollowing_t` result (callback `345`) within a bounded timeout. It never calls `SteamAPI_Init` (no second init / DLL conflict) and resolves all Steam symbols at runtime, so **no Steamworks SDK is needed at build time**. Capability order: `steamworks.js` friends API → native addon → manual self-attest. When no automatic check is available (addon absent, Steam absent, or no logged-in user) `followCheckSupported` is `false`, the UI offers a persisted manual claim, and the launcher never fabricates a follow.

## Prerequisites

- **Windows 10/11 x64** with the **Steam client installed**.
- A **Steam account**: one that will follow the developer account, and the developer's **SteamID64**.
- **Visual Studio Build Tools** (Desktop development with C++) + **Python 3** + Node.js (repo version) + `node-gyp` (bundled with npm). No Steamworks SDK is required to build the addon.
- Repo checked out at the validated commit on `dev` (or a release tag).
- **Private config** (never committed): either `electron/steam-config.local.json` with `app_id` + `developer_steam_id` (copy the shape from `electron/steam-config.example.json`), or env vars `TCE_STEAM_APP_ID` / `TCE_STEAM_DEVELOPER_STEAM_ID`.
- A **test App ID the account can run** (e.g. `480` "Spacewar" for local dev) and a build/depot the account may publish to if using the SteamPipe path (Part C2).

## Part A — Build the native addon

1. Install JS deps at the repo root: `npm ci` (or `npm install`).
2. Build + stage the addon:
   ```
   npm run build:steam-friends
   ```
   - Runs `node-gyp rebuild` in `native/steam-friends` (targets the Node/Electron ABI).
   - Stages the binary as `node_modules/tce-steam-friends/build/Release/steam_friends.node`.
   - Expected output: `[steam] staged native friends addon at …`.
   - On a non-Windows host it warns and skips (expected).
3. Verify the staged module:
   - `node_modules	ce-steam-friends\build\Release\steam_friends.node` exists.
   - `node_modules	ce-steam-friends\package.json` has `"main": "build/Release/steam_friends.node"`.
   - *(Sanity only)* a bare `node -e "require('tce-steam-friends').init()"` returns `false` outside the launcher — expected, because `steam_api64.dll` is only loaded once `steamworks.js` initialises inside the Electron main process.

If `node-gyp` fails, fix the toolchain (MSVC workload / Python) and re-run; record the exact error.

## Part B — Build and package the Steam launcher

4. Install the optional SDK binding: `npm install steamworks.js`.
5. Package:
   ```
   npm run package:steam
   ```
   - Pre-flight runs `scripts/check-steamworks.mjs` then `scripts/check-steam-friends.mjs`; **both must pass on Windows**.
   - Produces the NSIS installer and `release\win-unpacked\` (the primary Steam artifact).
6. Confirm the addon was packed and unpacked from the asar, e.g.:
   - `release\win-unpackedesources\app.asar.unpacked
ode_modules	ce-steam-friends\build\Release\steam_friends.node`
   - If it is missing, the asar globs/`asarUnpack` in `electron-builder.yml` need fixing (record as a defect).

## Part C — Make it available in the local Steam client

Choose **C1** for a quick local pass, or **C2** for a true "installed from the Steam library" run.

### C1 — Add a Non-Steam Game (fast, no upload)

1. Start the Steam client and log in.
2. Library → **Add a Game** → **Add a Non-Steam Game…** → **Browse** → select `release\win-unpacked\Tableau Card Engine.exe` → **Add Selected Programs**.
3. Ensure the app learns a usable App ID: put `steam_appid.txt` containing the test App ID (e.g. `480`) next to the executable (or set `TCE_STEAM_APP_ID`), so `SteamAPI_Init` succeeds.
4. Launch the game **from the Steam library** (not from the filesystem) so a Steam user context exists.
5. Caveat: a non-Steam launch has no real App ID/ownership. `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` only needs a logged-in user context, but if `restartAppIfNecessary` causes a relaunch loop, use C2.

### C2 — SteamPipe dev build (real App ID, installed from the library)

1. Prepare SteamPipe config (never commit real IDs; keep them local):
   - `steam/app_build_<appid>.vdf`:
     ```vdf
     "AppBuild"
     {
       "AppID" "<appid>"
       "Desc" "TCE follow-detection validation"
       "BuildOutput" "..\build-output\"
       "ContentRoot" "..elease\win-unpacked\"
       "SetLive" "validation"
       "Preview" "0"
       "Local" ""
       "Depots"
       {
         "<depotid>"
         {
           "File" "depot_build_<depotid>.vdf"
         }
       }
     }
     ```
   - `steam/depot_build_<depotid>.vdf`:
     ```vdf
     "DepotBuild"
     {
       "DepotID" "<depotid>"
       "ContentRoot" "..elease\win-unpacked\"
       "FileMapping"
       {
         "LocalPath" "*"
         "DepotPath" "."
         "recursive" "1"
       }
       "FileExclusion" "*.pdb"
     }
     ```
2. Upload to a **beta branch** (leaves the default branch untouched):
   ```
   steamcmd +login <build_account> +run_app_build "..\steam\app_build_<appid>.vdf" +quit
   ```
3. In the Steam client: app **Properties → Betas → Beta Participation** → select `validation`.
4. **Install / Update** the app from the library and wait for the download to finish.
5. Launch from the library.

Verify the client is running the addon build (Part B step 6 path exists inside the install dir).

## Part D — Validation matrix

Record **Pass / Fail / N-A** and evidence (screenshot, console output, or note) for each row. UI/console helper: `await window.tce.steamFollow.supportsAutomaticFollowCheck()` via DevTools.

| # | Scenario | Steps | Expected |
|---|----------|-------|----------|
| D1 | Addon loaded / capability true | Logged in, following the dev account; open the follow CTA / call `supportsAutomaticFollowCheck()` | `true`; UI offers automatic detection; no crash |
| D2 | Automatic detection — positive | Follow the developer account, then trigger the follow re-check | Bonus (`bonusGameId` in `electron/bonus-catalog.json`, currently *Feudalism*) unlocks; **no manual claim** |
| D3 | Automatic detection — negative | Do **not** follow, then re-check | Bonus stays locked; no fabricated unlock |
| D4 | Not logged in | Steam running, no user logged in; launch | Boots; no crash; `isFollowing` returns `false`; bonus locked; manual claim available |
| D5 | Steam absent | Quit Steam; launch | Boots with a clear "Steam unavailable" warning; bonus locked; every non-gated game playable |
| D6 | Persistence | After a successful unlock, close and relaunch | Still unlocked; no re-prompt; no follow re-check on boot |
| D7 | Manual-claim fallback | Remove/rename `node_modules	ce-steam-friends` in the installed app; relaunch | `followCheckSupported === false`; manual self-attest claim still unlocks |
| D8 | Browser fallback | Open the web build in a plain browser | No bridge; nothing locked; app fully functional |
| D9 | Store page | Click "Follow us on Steam" | Store/community page opens inside the Steam client/overlay, already logged in; no crash |
| D10 | Regression (no Steam needed) | At the validated commit: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/steam-follow/`; `npm run build` | All green |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The addon builds on Windows x64 and `npm run package:steam` passes its pre-flights.
- [ ] The packaged artifact contains the unpacked `tce-steam-friends` `.node`.
- [ ] The launcher runs from the local Steam client with a logged-in account.
- [ ] With the account following the developer, `followCheckSupported === true` and the designated bonus unlocks automatically (no manual claim) — D1/D2.
- [ ] Not-logged-in and Steam-absent launches do not crash, do not fabricate a follow, keep the bonus locked, and keep base games playable — D4/D5.
- [ ] The unlock persists across relaunch without re-verification — D6.
- [ ] Manual-claim (D7), browser (D8) and store-page (D9) paths behave as specified.
- [ ] `tests/steam-follow/` unit tests and `npm run build` pass at the validated commit — D10.
- [ ] Evidence is recorded as a comment on this item, and the outcome is reflected on P6 `CG-0MUNBI08A001D0XU` and the parent `CG-0MUN7930Y009X8Z1`.

## Out of Scope

- Native addon builds for macOS/Linux (Windows x64 only).
- A publisher-backend / Steam Web API follow check.
- Steam achievements validation (separate epic).

## Deliverables

- Completed validation matrix with evidence (screenshots / console / notes).
- A summary comment; any defects found become linked work items (blocking this item if they prevent a pass).

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md`
- `native/steam-friends/README.md`
- `docs/dev/steam-follow-native-spike.md`

# Intake Brief: Visual storyline authoring editor (core)

**Recreated in the core repo.** This epic was moved from `tce-main-street`
(`MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19`, deleted on migration) because the story-line engine now
lives in core (`src/story-line/`, shipped by `CG-0MVH2H67H002M27B`). The
original producer decisions are carried forward unchanged: **Q1 = A (in-repo
local web tool)**, **Q2 = A (epic decomposed into vertical slices)**, **Q3 = A
(curated form/guided editor)**.

## Problem statement

The branching story-line mechanic is now a first-class core module
(`src/story-line/`: types, `compile`, `resolve`, `journal`, `ui-adapter`, plus
the `@story-line` alias and the Gym `GymStorylineScene` demo). What did **not**
move is authoring: the content CSV model, the transactional author API, the
static validator and the manifest/Mermaid graph generator are still
Main-Street-only code (`tce-main-street` `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`,
`validate-storylines.ts`, `storyline-graph.ts`, `render-storyline-graph.ts`)
wired to Main Street card columns (coins/reputation deltas, `storylineId`,
`storylineTitle`).

Consequently a content designer for **any** TCE game that uses story-lines can
still only hand-edit a game-local CSV or drive a game-local CLI, and can only
see the arc as a generated Mermaid/JSON/`SVG` artefact. They cannot *see* the arc
they are editing, cannot discover dangling targets visually, and cannot make a
guided, validated edit in one place.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers (any TCE game)** — see a storyline's shape at
  a glance, inspect a card's links and metadata, and make guided edits (rename,
  retarget a link, regroup a storyline, add a card) without touching CSV
  internals.
- **TCE core engineers** — trust that every edit goes through one validated,
  transactional write path and that committed artefacts stay in sync with the
  game's content CSV.
- **Future tooling authors** — reuse an editor/view-model seam that reads the
  manifest rather than re-parsing the CSV.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to open a local tool, see the storyline graph
  rendered from the manifest, and click a card to inspect its links, so I can
  understand an arc before changing it."
- "As a content designer, I want to edit a card's name, effect and successor
  links in a form and see a preview plus validation errors, so I cannot write a
  dangling chain."
- "As a content designer, I want the committed graph and manifest regenerated
  automatically after an accepted edit, so the docs never drift from content."
- "As a game developer, I want the editor to be a local dev tool driven by my
  game's content adapter, excluded from the game build and reusing the same
  author API, so it adds no runtime dependency and no second CSV write path."

## Scope areas

### 0. Content and authoring toolchain generalised into core (prerequisite)

The editor must not depend on Main-Street-only code, so the authoring seams the
original epic assumed are part of this epic's scope:

1. A generic **content model** over the core story-line types: parse/serialise
   the game content CSV, a **content adapter** seam for game-specific columns
   (Main Street's coins/reputation deltas, `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`,
   `hasChoices`/accept/reject), and a content checksum for change detection.
2. A generic **manifest builder** and Mermaid **graph generator** (deterministic,
   timestamp-free) producing the same node/edge/storyline/cycle shape the
   editor's view model consumes.
3. A generic **static validator** with a formattable report (cycles
   informational, opt-in failure on cycle).
4. A generic **transactional author API**: build the edited CSV in memory,
   validate, then write atomically; `--dry-run` supported; the **only** writer.
5. Thin `tsx` CLIs over each seam (core tooling runs on `tsx`, not `vite-node`).

Parity requirement: extracting these seams must not change Main Street's shipped
storylines or CSV formats; the existing Main-Street storyline suites stay green
while it migrates onto the core seams.

### A. Editor host and read-only graph viewer

6. A local web tool launched with `npm run storylines:editor` from the repo
   root, built on the existing Vite toolchain (no new runtime dependency). It is
   a development tool and must not be included in the game or Electron build.
   The tool takes the game's content CSV / adapter as a launch argument so it is
   game-agnostic.
7. An interactive, manifest-driven graph view: storyline grouping, choice cards
   distinguished from plain incidents, cycle edges marked, pan/zoom and node
   selection. Read-only in the first slice.

### B. Transactional write bridge

8. A Node-side bridge over the core author/validator/graph seams: preview/diff
   before write, validate-before-write, artefact regeneration after an accepted
   edit, and a concurrency guard (content hash).

### C. Curated form/guided editing UX

9. Edit an existing card's fields through the content adapter's generic field
   descriptors (core-editable: name, effect text, choice flag, accept/reject
   successor links, storyline id/title; game columns such as coin/reputation
   deltas come from the adapter).
10. Add a new card and link it into a storyline through a guided form; discard
    pending (unwritten) changes before committing.

### D. Storyline management, docs and tests

11. Storyline-level operations (create/rename a `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`
    group and reassign member cards) driven through the same author API.
12. Documentation covering launch, the viewer, the edit workflow, validation and
    artefact regeneration (core engine reference + developer tooling docs), and
    the note in `tce-main-street` that its authoring tooling now consumes core.
13. Unit tests for the view-model/API bridge and a browser (Playwright) test for
    the viewer and a representative edit round-trip.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Editor launches locally** — `npm run storylines:editor -- --help` exits 0
   from the core repo root on the existing toolchain with no new runtime
   dependency; the command is documented in the core docs. Verified by a test
   that invokes the entry point and asserts it exits 0.
2. **Game-agnostic content source** — the editor loads a game's content CSV and
   field mapping through the content adapter; no Main Street import appears in
   the editor or the core authoring seams. Verified by a unit test over a
   synthetic fixture plus an import-boundary check.
3. **Manifest-driven interactive graph** — the editor renders the generated
   manifest: all nodes and edges appear, choice cards are visually distinct,
   storyline grouping and cycle edges are shown, and selecting a node shows its
   links/metadata. Covered by a browser test.
4. **Read-only fidelity** — the editor's view model (nodes, edges, storyline
   ids/titles, cycle flags) matches the generated manifest exactly; verified by
   a unit test that diffs the view model against the manifest and its JSON
   schema.
5. **Curated editing via the author API only** — the editor can edit the fields
   in Scope C and add a card; every mutation is routed through the core author
   API. A test asserts no editor module writes the content CSV except through
   that module, and a round-trip test proves an edited fixture validates.
6. **Preview and validate-before-write** — every edit shows a preview/diff and
   runs the validator before writing; an invalid edit exits non-zero, writes
   nothing, and surfaces the offending card/link. Covered by unit tests against
   valid and deliberately broken edits.
7. **Artefacts regenerated on accepted edit** — after an accepted edit the tool
   regenerates the committed Mermaid/JSON manifest artefacts (and any generated
   per-game doc artefacts the game opts into), and the `--check` drift guards
   pass. Edits that touch hand-written documented rows surface an explicit
   "manual documentation update required" result naming the failing check.
   Covered by tests.
8. **Concurrency guard** — if the content CSV changed on disk since load, the
   editor refuses to write and instructs the author to reload. Covered by a
   unit test.
9. **Build excluded** — the editor assets/entry are not part of the production
   game bundle or the packaged Electron app; verified by a build/test assertion
   (the editor entry is not referenced from the game `index.html`/`main.ts`
   graph).
10. **All related documentation is updated** — core engine reference, developer
    tooling docs, code comments, and the Main Street note that its authoring
    tooling consumes the core seams.
11. **Full project test suite must pass** — `npm test`
   (`scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`: unit + browser + tutorial E2E + Electron smoke)
    is green, and the Main Street storyline suites stay green.

## Constraints

- **Single write path** — one transactional, self-validating author operation in
  core; no second way to edit content CSVs.
- **No new runtime dependency** — reuse the existing Vite/`tsx`/Vitest/Playwright
  toolchain; the generic module stays Phaser-free and game-import-free.
- **Consumable by games** — core ships the seams and a default content adapter;
  games supply their own adapter (column mapping) and content CSV.
- **Deterministic artefacts** — manifest/Mermaid generators must stay
  timestamp-free so existing drift guards keep passing.
- **Development tool, not shipped** — the editor must not be pulled into the
  production game build or the packaged Electron app.
- **Behaviour preservation** — extraction must not change Main Street's shipped
  storylines (tax, health, economy, labour, restaurant) or CSV formats; RNG seed
  replays stay identical.
- **Preserve designed tension** — the editor is an authoring tool; it must not
  alter player-facing content semantics or reveal escalation content to players.
- **UK English** in all UI copy and documentation.
- **Scope guard** — conditional/cost-gated option semantics
  (`MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9`) stay out of scope; the editor edits today's curated
  choice model. Record extra opportunities as linked work items.

## Existing state (core repo research, verified)

- **Generic runtime** — `src/story-line/` (`compile.ts`, `resolve.ts`,
  `journal.ts`, `ui-adapter.ts`, `types.ts`, `index.ts`), exported through the
  `@story-line` alias (`resolveCoreAliases`, `tsconfig.json`, scaffold template).
  Generic CSV `options` encoding and legacy `hasChoices` compilation already
  exist here; there is **no** manifest, validator, author or graph seam.
- **Tests** — `tests/story-line/{compile,resolve,journal,ui-adapter}.test.ts`
  with `tests/story-line/helpers.ts` (in-memory engine-adapter double, no game
  dependency).
- **Docs** — `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (module, adapters, Gym demo).
- **Demo** — `example-games/gym/scenes/GymStorylineScene.ts` (registered, smoke
  covered).
- **Tooling conventions** — core CLIs are `tsx` scripts under `scripts/`
  (`npx tsx scripts/...`) and `npm test` runs `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  (unit → browser → tutorial E2E → Electron smoke); Vitest projects `unit`
  (`tests/**/*.test.ts`) and `browser` (`tests/**/*.browser.test.ts`) are
  configured in the root `vite.config.ts`. `ajv` and Playwright are existing
  devDependencies.
- **Gap** — no authoring toolchain in core; Main Street still owns the only
  author/validator/manifest/graph implementations.
- **Source of the seams to generalise** — `tce-main-street`
  `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` (`parseCsv`, `addCard`, `linkCard`,
  `applyToFile`, `parseAuthorArgs`), `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`
  (`validateStorylines`, `formatStorylineReport`, `storylineReportToJson`),
  `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` (`buildStorylineManifest`,
  `serializeManifest`, `renderMermaid`, `filterManifestByStoryline`,
  `nodeLabel`, `briefEventDescription`, `describeEventImpact`,
  `describeChoiceRouting`), `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph.ts`,
  `src/CsvChecksum.ts` (`computeCsvChecksum`), and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`.

## Desired change

1. **Generalise** the content/authoring seams into core behind a content
   adapter, with parity tests against the Main Street behaviour.
2. **Host a local editor** — `npm run storylines:editor` serves an in-repo dev
   page backed by a small Node-side API bridge over the author/validator/graph
   seams.
3. **Interactive viewer** — render the manifest graph with storyline grouping,
   choice/plain distinction, cycle marking, pan/zoom/select.
4. **Guided editing** — edit card fields and add/relink cards through forms that
   preview the diff and validate before write.
5. **Stay in sync** — regenerate the committed artefacts after accepted edits
   and guard against concurrent external CSV edits.
6. **Document and test** — authoring walkthrough, unit tests for the
   bridge/view-model and a browser round-trip test.

**Recommended slice order for planning** (per Q2 = A): (S0) generalise the
content/authoring toolchain → (S1) host + read-only viewer → (S2) write bridge +
preview/validate → (S3) curated edit forms → (S4) storyline management +
docs/tests polish.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/content/types.ts` — **new** generic content model + adapter
  seam.
- `src/story-line/content/csv.ts` — **new** parse/serialise + content checksum.
- `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts` — **new** manifest builder + Mermaid
  generator.
- `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` — **new** validator + report formatting.
- `src/story-line/content/author.ts` — **new** transactional author API.
- `scripts/storyline-author.ts` — **new** `tsx` CLI over the author API.
- `scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — **new** `tsx` CLI over the manifest generator.
- `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — **new** `tsx` CLI over the validator.
- `scripts/storyline-editor-cli.ts` — **new** editor entry point.
- `scripts/storyline-editor-server.ts` — **new** host + API bridge.
- `src/story-line/editor/view-model.ts` — **new** manifest → view model.
- `tools/storyline-editor/` — **new** editor page + SVG graph renderer.
- `tests/story-line/editor/` — **new** unit + browser tests and fixtures.
- `./vite.editor.config.ts` — **new** dedicated editor host config (does not
  touch the game/build config).
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — **edit** authoring + editor sections.
- `docs/dev/storyline-editor.md` — **new** developer/content-designer
  walkthrough.
- `./package.json` — **edit** add the `storylines:*` scripts.

## Migration notes and assumptions

- **Why moved** — the runtime engine now ships from core
  (`CG-0MVH2H67H002M27B` / `CSS-…` extraction round), so an editor for it belongs
  with the engine, not with one game.
- **Assumption: the authoring toolchain must be generalised first.** Only the
  runtime module moved; the author/validator/manifest/graph code is still
  Main-Street-only. Child T0 was added for this (it did not exist in the original
  plan) and blocks the viewer work. If the producer would rather keep the
  authoring toolchain game-side, this epic collapses back to a Main Street tool.
- **Assumption: game-specific columns stay in the game adapter.** Core edits the
  generic story-line fields; coin/reputation deltas and other game columns are
  described by the game's adapter. Main Street's existing behaviour (and its
  `set-storyline` gap: the CLI documents it but implements only `add-card` and
  `link`, so storyline assignment goes through `linkCard`'s
  `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`) is preserved by parity tests.
- **Assumption: toolchain** — core CLIs use `tsx` (not `vite-node`), and the
  editor's content source is a path argument, so the Main Street `?raw` CSV
  import constraint does not apply.
- **Effort/risk inherited** from the original item (`Severe` risk, `Large`
  effort). The S0 prerequisite adds scope, so both should be re-run with
  `/skill:effort-and-risk` before implementation starts.
- **Original item** `MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19` and its six children
  (`MS-0MUSY1K6B00095AT`, `MS-0MUSY1M1F003IS47`, `MS-0MUSY1O8V008F9BO`,
  `MS-0MUSY1QAS007AREL`, `MS-0MUSY1S54000GPIT`, `MS-0MUSY1UIR007XLOQ`) were
  deleted from the `tce-main-street` worklog in the same change; all content was
  carried into this tree.

## Related work

- **CG-0MVH2H67H002M27B** — "Generic story-line system in core (module, parity
  tests, Gym demo, docs)" — the extraction this epic follows.
- **CG-0MVHY82PQ004Q3B9** — "Manually test the story-line extraction (Gym demo +
  Main Street storylines)".
- `tce-main-street` `MS-0MVCRQ475009CDZI` — "Extract the storyline features"

# Pin the Phaser-free `@ui` node import surface as a machine-checked contract

**Headline:** The `@ui` barrel is Phaser-bearing by design, so downstream game
unit suites must import deep Phaser-free paths. Today that rule lives only in
prose (plus an evaluation-based test guard) and names a handful of modules
incidentally. This item pins the surface explicitly — a typed, machine-readable
manifest of modules guaranteed importable in a Node environment with no
`window` — and enforces it with a static import-graph check that fails when a
listed module transitively reaches a Phaser **value** import, without depending
on test execution order.

## Problem statement

`CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ` fixed the immediate regression (a Phaser value import
leaking into `illegalMoveToastView` and, through it, `@ui/shakeIllegalMove` and
`@ui/dragDrop`) and added a Node-environment guard
(`tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts`) that imports each framework-free entry
point under a throwing `phaser` mock. What remains missing is a *contract*:

- There is no canonical, machine-readable statement of **which** `src/ui`
  modules are node-safe. `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
  (§ "Phaser-free `@ui` helper imports for Node tests", ~line 1817) names four
  modules in prose and adds "other `@ui` modules (e.g. `@ui/screen-layout`,
  `@ui/constants`) are also Phaser-free. When in doubt, probe with a readonly
  `vite-node` import" — i.e. the guidance for the common case is *empirical
  probing*, not a lookup.
- The only enforcement is **evaluation-based** (the module actually has to be
  imported inside a Vitest file for the mock to fire). A listed module that is
  never imported by the guard, or a listing added later, is silently unguarded.
  The guard also cannot distinguish "listed module is safe" from "listed module
  is untested".
- The barrel caveat (`@ui` itself is Phaser-bearing because
  `CardGameScene extends Phaser.Scene`) is documented, but only as prose inside
  one developer-guide section; nothing at the barrel's own definition site says
  "never import this from a Node test".

## Users and user stories

- **Downstream game producer/agent:** "As a producer in a `tce-<game>` repo, I
  can look up whether a given `@ui` module is safe to import from a Node unit
  test instead of running an ad-hoc `vite-node` probe and hoping I read the
  crash correctly."
- **Engine maintainer:** "As an engine maintainer, when I add a Phaser value
  import (or a `./Renderer` import) to a module on the node-safe list, a core
  check fails immediately and names the module and the offending import chain —
  not 23 downstream suites with `window is not defined` (`CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ`)."
- **Engine maintainer growing the surface:** "As an engine maintainer, adding a
  module to the guaranteed surface is one edit to one list, and the check proves
  the new entry actually satisfies the contract before it is promised."
- **Game scene author (unchanged behaviour):** "As a scene author I keep
  importing whatever `@ui` path I like from scene code; nothing about runtime
  behaviour, animation, or the barrel's exports changes."

## Existing state (evidence, verified read-only in this intake)

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § *Phaser-free `@ui` helper imports for Node tests*
  (line ~1817) already states the rule, the barrel caveat, the guard file, and
  cross-links this item (`CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN`). It is prose only — no list
  exists in code.
- `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts` exists and guards exactly four deep
  entry points (`illegalMoveToastView`, `shakeIllegalMove`, `dragDrop`,
  `illegalMoveToast`) with a file-scoped throwing `vi.mock('phaser')` plus a
  negative control (`@ui/Renderer`). Its module docblock already points at this
  item for "the broader documented Phaser-free node surface + static import-graph
  check".
- A read-only regex import-graph probe over `src/ui/*.ts` in this intake found
  **44** modules with no transitive Phaser value import and **18** Phaser-bearing
  ones (`CardGameScene`, `createCardGame`, `GameSelectorScene`, `HelpPanel`,
  `HelpButton`, `SettingsPanel`, `SettingsButton`, `SceneHeader`, `HighlightManager`,
  `HintBar`, `Slider`, `Tooltip`, `hiDpiText`, `versionDisplay`, `AlphaBadge`,
  `CardPackListing`, `GymSceneUtils`, `index`). The probe was **regex-based and
  approximate** (it does not follow `@core-engine/*` / `@card-system/*` /
  `@rule-engine/*` / `@ai/*` / `@ui/*` path aliases, `export * from`, or dynamic
  `import()`), so the real numbers must come from the new compiler-based check.
  That gap is itself evidence for building the check rather than trusting a
  hand-written list.
- Sibling repos exist locally (`../tce-beleaguered-castle`, `../tce-blackjack`,
  `../tce-coloretto`, `../tce-feudalism`, `../tce-golf`,
  `../tce-lost-cities`, `../tce-main-street`, `../tce-sushi-go`,
  `../tce-the-rising`, …). A read-only census of their deep `@ui/...` imports
  shows the framework-free modules they actually reach for are a small,
  identifiable set (`@ui/screen-layout*`, `@ui/constants`, `@ui/SettingsStore`,
  `@ui/dragDrop`, `@ui/shakeIllegalMove`, `@ui/PileView`, `@ui/Overlay`,
  `@ui/game-plugin-boot`, `@ui/card-pack-client`, `@ui/card-pack-url`,
  `@ui/content-unlock-client`, `@ui/CardPackLoader`, `@ui/popTextOrIcon`,
  `@ui/moveGameObject`, `@ui/discardCard`), while the rest of their usage is
  scene-only (`@ui/createCardGame`, `@ui/Renderer*`, `@ui/CardGameScene`,
  `@ui/HelpPanel`, `@ui/Tooltip`, `@ui/debug/*`).
- Tooling precedent for repo checks exists: `scripts/check-terminology-guards.sh`,
  `scripts/check-browser-test-env.ts`, `scripts/check-steamworks.mjs`, plus
  `tests/scripts/*.test.ts` unit coverage for each script. `typescript` (5.9.3)
  is already a dev dependency, so a compiler-API check needs **no new
  dependency**.
- No existing item covers this: `wl search` over *phaser*, *node-safe*,
  *import guard*, *window is not defined*, *ui barrel* returns
  `CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ` (the fix that **caused** the follow-up and explicitly
  defers option C here) and `CG-0MVPXFHBZ004LGEB` (the toast feature). No
  duplicate; this item is the deferred remainder.

## Desired change

1. **Typed manifest (single source of truth).** Add
   `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` exporting a readonly, `as const` list of the
   `src/ui` module paths guaranteed to be importable in a Node environment (no
   `window`, no Phaser evaluation), each with a one-line rationale comment
   (what it is / why it must stay framework-free). The file must itself be
   Phaser-free and side-effect-free (a plain data module) so it can be imported
   by the check, the guard test and docs tooling. Candidate initial entries
   (each to be **verified** by the new check during implementation, not assumed):
   `illegalMoveToast`, `illegalMoveToastView`, `shakeIllegalMove`, `dragDrop`,
   `screen-layout`, `screen-layout-compose`, `screen-layout-schema`,
   `constants`, `SettingsStore`, `card-pack-url`, `card-pack-client`,
   `game-asset-url`, `game-manifest`, `game-plugin-boot`, `content-unlock-client`.
2. **Static import-graph check.** Add `scripts/check-ui-node-surface.ts`
   (TypeScript compiler API — `typescript` is already a devDependency; no new
   package) that, for **every** entry in the manifest:
   - resolves and walks the module graph from that entry using the same
     `paths`/aliases as `tsconfig.json` (so `@core-engine/*`, `@card-system/*`,
     `@rule-engine/*`, `@ai/*`, `@ui/*` are followed, not skipped);
   - ignores **type-only** imports and re-exports
     (`import type`, `export type`, `import { type X }`), which are elided at
     compile time and cannot evaluate Phaser;
   - treats a resolved `phaser` specifier reached through a **value** edge as a
     violation, and reports the full offending chain
     (`src/ui/X.ts → src/ui/Y.ts → phaser`);
   - exits `0` when every listed module is clean, non-zero with one line per
     violation (module, chain) otherwise; supports `--json` for tests;
   - is a total function over inputs: an unresolvable specifier inside
     `src/ui`/aliases is itself a violation (never a silent skip), and a listed
     module that does not exist is a violation.
   Wire it as `npm run check:ui-node-surface` and include it in the
   pre-implementation gate used by `implement.py finish` / the dev-push path
   (resolved: Q2 → A, hard gate).
3. **Extend the guard test to the manifest.** `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts`
   keeps its throwing-mock + negative control, but iterates the manifest so
   adding an entry automatically gets an evaluation-based guard too — the two
   mechanisms are complementary (static graph check = complete coverage and
   order independence; throwing mock = proof that the runtime actually starts
   without Phaser).
4. **Docs + barrel comment.** `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § *Phaser-free `@ui` helper
   imports for Node tests* gains the manifest as the authoritative list (link +
   the "adding a module" procedure), states the check and its npm script, and
   replaces "when in doubt, probe with `vite-node`" with "look it up in the
   manifest; if it is not listed, treat it as Phaser-bearing". `src/ui/index.ts`
   gains a short docblock above `UI_VERSION` stating explicitly that the barrel
   is **intentionally** Phaser-bearing (`CardGameScene extends Phaser.Scene`),
   that Node tests must import deep Phaser-free paths, and pointing at the
   manifest + check. `docs/ui-animations.md` node-safe note gains the same
   pointer.

Non-goals: no change to any runtime behaviour, public signature, barrel export
list, or `src/ui/constants.ts` value; no attempt to make the whole of `src/ui`
node-safe; no sibling-repo edits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` exists, is Phaser-free and side-effect-free,
      and exports a typed readonly manifest of node-safe `src/ui` module paths
      with a one-line rationale per entry; every listed entry was verified by
      the new check (not assumed from a regex probe).
- [ ] `scripts/check-ui-node-surface.ts` walks the real import graph for every
      manifest entry (following the `tsconfig.json` path aliases), ignores
      type-only edges, and exits non-zero naming the module and the offending
      chain when a listed module transitively has a **value** import of
      `phaser` or of a Phaser-bearing module such as `src/ui/Renderer`.
- [ ] The check is **proved to have teeth**: unit tests in
      `tests/scripts/check-ui-node-surface.test.ts` cover (a) a clean manifest
      exiting 0, (b) a value `import Phaser from 'phaser'` entry failing with the
      offending path in the output, (c) a transitive failure through an alias
      (`@core-engine/*` or `@ui/*`), (d) a **type-only** Phaser import passing,
      (e) an unresolvable specifier failing closed, (f) a missing listed module
      failing, and (g) the real repo manifest passing (a live regression gate).
- [ ] `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts` iterates the manifest so every
      listed module is imported at runtime under the throwing `phaser` mock,
      keeping its negative control (`@ui/Renderer` fails, mock call count
      increases) so the guard cannot silently pass.
- [ ] `npm run check:ui-node-surface` is wired into the implementation gate
      (per Q2) and runs green on a clean tree; a deliberately introduced Phaser
      value import in a listed module makes it fail (documented in the item
      comment with the command output).
- [ ] `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents the manifest as the authoritative node-safe
      list, the check + npm script, and the "adding a module to the surface"
      procedure, and retires the "probe with `vite-node` when in doubt" advice in
      favour of the lookup; `src/ui/index.ts` carries a docblock stating the
      barrel is intentionally Phaser-bearing and that Node tests must import
      deep Phaser-free paths; `docs/ui-animations.md` links the manifest.
      Code comments cross-link `CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN`.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] `npm run build` (TypeScript strict + Vite) succeeds.

## Constraints

- **No new dependencies:** the check uses the TypeScript compiler API
  (`typescript`, already a devDependency). Do not add an AST/lexer package.
- **Core-only:** no edits to sibling `tce-<game>` repos. Sibling findings are
  read-only evidence and, at most, a note in this item.
- **No behaviour change:** nothing in `src/ui` runtime code changes except the
  `index.ts` docblock. If a candidate manifest entry turns out to be
  Phaser-bearing, **drop it from the manifest** rather than editing that module
  to accommodate the list (changing a module's import graph is a separate item).
- **Type-only Phaser references stay legal** and must keep compiling under
  `isolatedModules` (`import type`).
- **The check must be deterministic and fast** (seconds, no bundler, no Vitest
  run, no network) so it can run on every push.
- **Fail closed:** an unresolvable specifier, a missing listed module, or a
  manifest file that cannot be parsed is a failure — never a warning.
- **Do not restructure the `@ui` barrel** or remove existing exports; scenes
  consume them today.
- Unit tests are the minimum gate during implementation; the full suite is
  required before the `dev` push.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` — NEW: the typed readonly manifest (~15 entries) + one-line rationale per entry; plain data, no imports.
- `scripts/check-ui-node-surface.ts` — NEW: TypeScript-compiler-API import-graph check over the manifest; alias-aware, type-only-eliding, fail-closed, `--json` output.
- `tests/scripts/check-ui-node-surface.test.ts` — NEW: teeth tests (clean / direct value import / transitive via alias / type-only OK / unresolvable / missing module / real-repo manifest).
- `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts` — Iterate the manifest instead of a hard-coded four-entry list; keep the throwing mock, the `phaserMock.calls === 0` assertion, and the `@ui/Renderer` negative control.
- `package.json` — NEW script `check:ui-node-surface`; wire into the gate chosen in Q2.
- `src/ui/index.ts` — Docblock above `UI_VERSION`: barrel is intentionally Phaser-bearing, Node tests import deep Phaser-free paths, link the manifest + check.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — § *Phaser-free `@ui` helper imports for Node tests*: manifest as the authoritative list, check + script, "adding a module" procedure, retire the probe-when-in-doubt advice.
- `docs/ui-animations.md` — Node-safe note under the `shakeIllegalMove` import block: point at the manifest.
- `AGENTS.md` — Only if the new npm script / gate changes developer workflow (Doc-Update Policy); otherwise no change.

## Risks and assumptions

- **False promise risk (medium):** listing a module as node-safe when it is not.
  Mitigation: every entry is verified by the new check during implementation;
  candidates that fail are dropped rather than patched.
- **Regex-probe trust risk (addressed):** the intake probe ignored path aliases,
  so the "44 Phaser-free" figure may be too high. Mitigation: the manifest starts
  deliberately narrow (the modules downstream node tests actually import plus the
  already-documented four) and grows only through verification.
- **Alias-resolution drift (medium):** the check must resolve aliases exactly as
  `vite.config.ts`/`tsconfig.json` do, or it will silently skip
  `@core-engine/*` edges. Mitigation: read `paths` from `tsconfig.json` (single
  source) and add the transitive-via-alias test case (AC 3c).
- **Maintenance burden (low–medium):** a listed module's author now has an extra
  constraint. Mitigation: narrow opt-in list + a failure message that names the
  module and chain, plus the "adding a module" procedure in the docs.
- **Check duplicating the guard (low):** two mechanisms could drift.
  Mitigation: both consume the same manifest, so they cannot disagree about
  *which* modules are promised.
- **Gate friction risk (medium):** adding a check to `implement.py finish` /
  pre-push could slow or block unrelated work if it is flaky. Mitigation: it is
  pure static analysis with no bundler/network, and Q2 asks the producer to
  choose whether it is a hard gate or a test-only check.
- **Scope-creep risk:** making all of `src/ui` node-safe, extracting a shared
  Phaser-free style builder (noted in `CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ`), or refactoring the
  barrel are **out of scope**; record them as separate items if they prove
  worthwhile.
- **Assumption:** the throwing-`phaser`-mock guard remains the runtime proof;
  this item only adds a *complete, order-independent* static complement, so the
  existing guard must not be weakened or removed.
- **Assumption:** no browser test asserts anything this item touches (docs and
  the barrel docblock only), so no browser suite change is expected.

## Resolved producer decisions

All three decisions were answered **A** (the recommended options), so the brief
above stands exactly as drafted; no AC changes were needed.

- **Q1 → A** — curated opt-in manifest (~15 entries; the modules downstream Node
  unit tests actually import, plus the four already documented). The check
  enforces the listed set; it is **not** a completeness snapshot of `src/ui`.
- **Q2 → A** — the static check is a **hard gate**: `npm run check:ui-node-surface`
  plus unit-test coverage, wired into the implementation / dev-push gate.
- **Q3 → A** — the manifest lives in `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` as a typed
  `as const` list with a one-line rationale per entry, consumed by both the
  check script and `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts`.

Confirmation status: **ready to plan** — no open questions remain.

## Related work

- **CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ** — "[test-failure] @ui barrel statically imports
  Phaser — downstream game unit suites fail with 'window is not defined'"
  (completed, shipped in v0.1.22): made `illegalMoveToastView` Phaser-free,
  added `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts`, documented the rule in
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` + `docs/ui-animations.md`, and **explicitly deferred**
  the documented surface + static import-graph check to this item.
- **CG-0MVPXFHBZ004LGEB** — "Core illegal-move routine: explain a rejected move
  with a reason toast" (completed): the change that introduced the regression,
  now fixed.
- **CG-0MSXKQVZC009AM9L** — "Play illegal move audio/visual when hand is full
  during buy" (completed): earlier consumer of the same shake/toast helper graph.
- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** — `tce-main-street` Bank Loans epic: was blocked by
  the regression; the sibling pin bump is tracked there, not here.
- Duplicate check performed (`wl search`: *phaser*, *node-safe*, *import guard*,
  *window is not defined*, *ui barrel*) — no item satisfies these ACs; the
  predecessor is the cause and defers option C here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Scope of the documented node-safe surface.** Options: (A) curated
  opt-in list of the `src/ui` modules that downstream Node unit tests actually
  import, plus the four already documented; (B) every `src/ui` module that is
  currently Phaser-free (approximate regex probe: 44 of 62 top-level modules),
  maintained as a snapshot; (C) prose list in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` only, no

  keep and covers the real consumer set; B promises node-safety for
  scene-coupled modules (`PileView`, `Overlay`, `HandView`, …) that nobody
  imports in Node, and C is what already exists and is not enforced.
  **Answer (producer):** **A** — curated opt-in list. Source: producer reply in this
  session ("1. A"). Effect: the manifest is scoped to the ~15 entries the
  downstream Node unit tests actually import plus the four already documented;
  the check enforces only the listed set (no completeness snapshot).
  Source: this intake session (auto-dispatched; no operator present). Effect
  once answered: A narrows the manifest to ~15 entries, B expands it to ~44 and
  makes the check a completeness snapshot, C removes the manifest and the
  manifest-driven guard extension.
- **Q2 — Enforcement of the static import-graph check.** Options: (A) hard gate:
  `npm run check:ui-node-surface` runs in the implementation/dev-push gate and
  the unit tests cover it; (B) test-only: the check is exercised only by
  `tests/scripts/check-ui-node-surface.test.ts` plus one real-repo assertion, no

  **Recommended:** A — the whole point of the follow-up is catching the
  regression *before* downstream suites do, and the check is pure static
  analysis (no bundler, no network, seconds).
  **Answer (producer):** **A** — hard gate. Source: producer reply in this session

  **Answer (producer):** **A** — typed TS module. Source: producer reply in this

# Teeth tests for the static import-graph check

**Goal:** Verify-before-implement — `tests/scripts/check-ui-node-surface.test.ts`
defines, through hermetic fixtures, the exact contract the static import-graph
check must satisfy, so the check (CG sibling impl item) is proven to have teeth
before it is promised. Parent: CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The test file covers all teeth cases from the parent AC 3:
      (a) a clean manifest exits 0;
      (b) a value `import Phaser from 'phaser'` entry fails with the offending
      path/module in the output;
      (c) a transitive failure through a path alias (`@core-engine/*` or
      `@ui/*`) fails and reports the full chain;
      (d) a **type-only** Phaser import passes (type-only edges are elided);
      (e) an unresolvable specifier inside `src/ui`/an alias fails closed
      (never a silent skip);
      (f) a listed module that does not exist fails;
      (g) the real repo manifest passes (a live regression gate).
- [ ] Fixtures are hermetic temp trees built by the tests themselves (injected
      via the check's `--manifest`/`--root` overrides), not checked-in fixture
      files that can drift.
- [ ] Tests run green under the unit profile and are deterministic (no network,
      no Vitest-in-Vitest, no bundler).
- [ ] Code comments cross-link CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN.


- [ ] The check is **proved to have teeth**: unit tests in
      `tests/scripts/check-ui-node-surface.test.ts` cover (a) a clean manifest
      exiting 0, (b) a value `import Phaser from 'phaser'` entry failing with the
      offending path in the output, (c) a transitive failure through an alias
      (`@core-engine/*` or `@ui/*`), (d) a **type-only** Phaser import passing,
      (e) an unresolvable specifier failing closed, (f) a missing listed module
      failing, and (g) the real repo manifest passing (a live regression gate).

## Minimal implementation

- Write `tests/scripts/check-ui-node-surface.test.ts` against the planned CLI
  contract: `--manifest <path>` (alters the entry list), `--root <dir>` (alters
  the base dir for resolution), `--json`, exit 0 clean / non-zero with one line
  per violation (module + chain).
- Each case creates a mini source tree in a temp dir (via `node:fs`, cleaned up
  in teardown) and invokes the check's exported API / CLI on it.
- Run the unit profile for the new test; expect red until the check is
  implemented (this is the contract-defining slice).

## Key files

- `tests/scripts/check-ui-node-surface.test.ts` — NEW: the seven teeth cases.

## Dependencies

- None to create first (defines the contract); the implementation it drives is
  the sibling "Static import-graph check" item — edge F3 → F2.

# Static import-graph check (TypeScript compiler API)

**Goal:** `scripts/check-ui-node-surface.ts` — a deterministic, seconds-fast,
compiler-based static check that walks the real import graph for every manifest
entry and fails when a listed module transitively reaches a Phaser **value**
import, so a reintroduced regression is caught here, not in 23 downstream game
suites with `window is not defined`. Parent: CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For every entry in the manifest, resolves and walks the module graph using
      the **same `paths`/aliases as `tsconfig.json`** (all of
      `@core-engine/*`, `@card-system/*`, `@rule-engine/*`, `@ai/*`, `@ui/*`
      are followed, not skipped).
- [ ] Ignores **type-only** imports and re-exports (`import type`,
      `export type`, `import { type X }`) — elided at compile time — while a
      resolved `phaser` specifier reached through a **value** edge is a
      violation reported with the full offending chain
      (`src/ui/X.ts → src/ui/Y.ts → phaser`).
- [ ] **Fail closed:** an unresolvable specifier inside `src/ui`/an alias, a
      listed module that does not exist, and an unparseable manifest file are
      each a violation (never a warning, never a silent skip).
- [ ] CLI contract: exits `0` when every listed module is clean; non-zero with
      one line per violation (module, chain); supports `--json` for tests;
      supports `--manifest <path>` / `--root <dir>` overrides for hermetic
      fixture tests.
- [ ] The real repo manifest passes (green); all cases in the teeth-test item
      pass. Uses only the TypeScript compiler API (`typescript` devDependency —
      **no new dependency**).
- [ ] Code comments cross-link CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN.


- [ ] `scripts/check-ui-node-surface.ts` walks the real import graph for every
      manifest entry (following the `tsconfig.json` path aliases), ignores
      type-only edges, and exits non-zero naming the module and the offending
      chain when a listed module transitively has a **value** import of
      `phaser` or of a Phaser-bearing module such as `src/ui/Renderer`.

## Minimal implementation

- Implement the compiler-API walker (resolve module specs via `tsconfig.json`
  `paths`; follow local + alias value edges; reject on `phaser` value edges).
- Add the CLI entry (`#!/usr/bin/env node`, argument parsing, exit codes).
- Run against the real manifest; iterate the teeth tests to green.

## Key files

- `scripts/check-ui-node-surface.ts` — NEW: the check.

## Dependencies

- Edge to the manifest item (consumes `uiNodeSafeModules`).
- Edge to the teeth-tests item (its passing tests are the contract).

# Manifest-driven node-import guard test

**Goal:** Extend `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts` so it iterates the
manifest — every listed module is imported at runtime under the throwing
`phaser` mock — while keeping its negative control, so adding a manifest entry
automatically gets an evaluation-based guard too (the runtime proof that
complements the static check). Parent: CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The guard imports **every** manifest entry under the file-scoped throwing
      `vi.mock('phaser')` (no hard-coded four-entry list); a manifest addition
      automatically widens the guard.
- [ ] Keeps the `phaserMock.calls === 0` assertion for all guard targets
      (Phaser never evaluated at import time).
- [ ] Keeps the negative control (`@ui/Renderer` fails under the same mock and
      the mock call count increases) so the guard cannot silently pass.
- [ ] The mock stays file-scoped (never moved into a global setup file).
- [ ] Runs green under the unit profile; code comments cross-link
      CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN.


- [ ] `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts` iterates the manifest so every
      listed module is imported at runtime under the throwing `phaser` mock,
      keeping its negative control (`@ui/Renderer` fails, mock call count
      increases) so the guard cannot silently pass.

## Minimal implementation

- Refactor `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts` to build its import list from
  `uiNodeSafeModules` (dynamic `import()` inside the test, asserting each
  namespace exports what the existing assertions expect where applicable).
- Keep the `@ui/Renderer` negative control unchanged in spirit.
- Run the unit profile for the file.

## Key files

- `tests/ui/phaser-free-imports.test.ts` — modified.
- `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` — consumed (depends on the manifest item).

## Dependencies

- Edge to the manifest item (consumes `uiNodeSafeModules`).
